rubric.principles_adherence: 0-3 — Applied relevant SOLID/YAGNI/KISS/DRY? 0=ignored, 1=mentioned, 2=applied, 3=applied with trade-off discussion
rubric.comment_quality: 0-3 — WHY-only comments? 0=narrative, 1=mixed, 2=mostly WHY, 3=WHY only or none needed

benchmark_schema.pass_threshold: All rubric items >= 2. Total >= 8/12 to pass.

evals.expected_output: Function renamed to describe behavior. Variables renamed with intent. Comments removed. Filter logic clarified or replaced with `.filter()`.
expectations: Function renamed (e.g., `filterValidEntries`)
Parameters and variables renamed (no `d`, `r`)
Narrative comments removed
Boolean check clarified (`d[i].v === true` → `entry.isValid` or similar)
No magic boolean without context

benchmarks.naming_rule_target: camelCase, descriptive, verb phrases for functions

evals.expected_output: Replace `readFileSync` with `fs.promises.readFile`. Add try/catch at boundary or let errors propagate. No sync I/O in async path.
expectations: Replaced `readFileSync` with async `fs.promises.readFile`
No synchronous I/O in the async function
Errors either propagated or handled at boundary
Uses `await` correctly

benchmarks.comment_rule_target: WHY only if explaining the event-loop constraint

evals.expected_output: Split by actor: validation (validator/DTO), hashing (auth service), persistence (repository), logging (logger service), email (notification service). Controller stays thin.
expectations: Validation extracted to its own unit
Password hashing moved to an auth service
DB access moved to a repository
Logging moved to a logger (async, structured)
Email moved to a notification service
Controller only orchestrates

evals.expected_output: YAGNI violation. The config options, plugin system, and middleware chain have zero callers. Start with a plain function or Node's built-in `EventEmitter`. Add complexity when a real need appears.
expectations: Identifies YAGNI violation
Recommends built-in EventEmitter or simple function
Flags unused config options and plugin system
Does not preserve speculative features

evals.expected_output: Move all env access to a single validated config module loaded at startup. Inject the config object into business logic. Fail fast if required vars are missing.
expectations: Env vars read once at startup, not scattered
Config validated with schema (zod/joi)
Typed config object injected, not process.env
Fails fast on missing required config

benchmarks.naming_rule_target: SCREAMING_SNAKE for env, camelCase for config

evals.expected_output: Swallowing errors with `catch { return null }` hides failures. Throw domain-specific errors, catch at the boundary (route handler), log with context, return appropriate HTTP status.
expectations: Identifies swallowed error anti-pattern
Recommends throwing or re-throwing with context
Domain-specific error classes suggested
Catch moved to boundary, not inside business logic

evals.expected_output: Flatten with guard clauses. Each validation returns early. The happy path (createUser + response) is at the base level.
expectations: Each validation is a guard clause with early return
Happy path at base indentation
No more than 1 level of nesting in the happy path
No else after returning if
Same validation behavior preserved
